title: Nightcap runbook scribbles — oncall 11pm-7am
content:
Quick context: I kicked off this scratchpad because tonight's traffic patterns looked noisy and the new batcher tuning (deployed last week) still feels brittle on long-tail seq lengths. Use this as a short-lived addendum to the main oncall playbook — stuff I want to remember between rotations and hand to next person.

Shift summary (11pm–7am):
- What I saw: 00:45 — intermittent 503s from hosted-api cluster a/b; roughly 1% error rate spike for ~20m.
- Root guesses at the time: routing fallback thrash between model-variants + transient GPU memory pressure on node pool dedicated-east-1b.
- Actions taken: scaled dedicated-east-1b by +2 instances (small GPU warm pool) at 00:50; triggered emergency fallback policy to degrade to smaller model variant for non-SLA routes; purged prefix cache on 1 node where logs showed KVcache mismatch.
- Outcome: errors dropped back to baseline (~0.05%) by 01:10, latency stable after 02:00.

Immediate open items for follow-up:
- Investigate why autoscaler didn't add capacity until manual scale. (Linked JIRA: JIRA-INF-412)
- KV cache purges were manual; we should test automated reconciliation flow in staging.
- Add an alert for repeated routing fallback cycles (>=3 within 5m).

Quick troubleshooting recipes (temp procedures)
Note: these are NOT final runbook steps — they are stopgap commands I used; validate before automating.

1) When you see 5xx spike (hosted-api):
- Check Alerts and Grafana first: panels -> Hosted API -> Error rate / Model fallback counts / GPU mem pressure.
- Slack: ping #incidents with a short summary: "5xx spike hosted-api a/b — investigating routing/fallback".
- Query to get recent fallback events (CLI):
  redwoodctl events query --service hosted-api --type routing-fallback --since 15m
- If fallback_count > 2 for same route: throttle non-critical routes via routing override:
  redwoodctl routing override apply --route /embed --policy static --model small-variant --duration 30m
- If GPU mem pressure on a node: tilt the node out of rotation and allow drain:
  kubectl cordon node/<node-id> && redwoodctl node drain --node <node-id> --grace 30s
- If multiple nodes show mem pressure, scale up warm pool:
  aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name dedicated-east-1b --desired-capacity <current+2>

2) KV cache mismatch / corrupted prefixes (what I did):
- Symptom: repeated token truncation errors, small spike of "kv-mismatch" logs on a single instance.
- Quick check: ssh to instance and tail logs: tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep kv-mismatch
- If confirmed on a single instance: purge local cache and restart runtime process (graceful):
  sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime && rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/kvcache/prefix-* && sudo systemctl start redwood-runtime
- Note: do NOT purge prefix cache globally unless you understand request heat — that will cause short-term latency spike.

3) Long queue backpressure (requests piling up):
- Symptoms: queue_size > 1000, avg latency rising but infra metrics show CPU/GPU not fully saturated.
- Quick action: increase batching window for the affected route to absorb short bursts:
  redwoodctl batching update --route /generate --window-ms 120 --max-batch 64
  (I set window-ms to 120 to trade10–30ms latency for increased throughput; revert later)
- If still backlogged: enable temporary cache-on-prefix for high-TPS prefixes:
  redwoodctl cache prefix add --route /generate --prefix "user:session:" --ttl 300s

Runbook drift notes (my assumptions + why these are provisional):
- Assumption A: the routing fallback thrash was caused by mis-specified health checks that intermittently mark instances unhealthy. Need to confirm with healthcheck logs.
- Assumption B: autoscaler did not trigger because the scaling policy uses p50 latency which stayed under threshold while p95 spiked; policy mismatch.
- Why provisional: I pulled a few logs and made quick config changes under pressure. These are band-aids — the proper fix needs a test+QA cycle.

Hand-off checklist for next oncall (what I will tell you in Slack when handing off):
- Check JIRA JIRA-INF-412 status — I created initial notes.
- Look at alerts: hosted-api 5xx SLO, routing-fallback count, gpu-mem-pressure.
- Review last 2 hours of routing events: redwoodctl events query --since 2h --service routing
- Verify dedicated-east-1b desired capacity is back to normal (I scaled +2) and annotate why in the autoscaling group's description.
- If you need to revert my caching/batching changes: I left a rollback snippet in the audit log (search for my username maya.chen).

Notes-to-self (for follow-ups / PRs):
- Create small automation to detect sequential fallback events and post to #incidents automatically (low effort).
- Add a unit test in autoscaler that compares p50 vs p95 signals used for scale triggers.
- Add a graceful kvcache reconciliation job in staging that safely validates prefixes before global purge.

Incidents & logs references (things I pulled):
- Hosted API error timeline: grafana/dashboard?id=hosted-api-errors&from=2026-03-05T00:30&to=2026-03-05T02:30
- Fallback events query: events.redwood.internal?service=routing&from=2026-03-05T00:00
- Node with mem pressure: dedicated-east-1b-node-17 (check node metrics, I left annotation in node tags)

Open questions I couldn't answer on shift:
- Is routing fallback implemented as a per-request or per-route policy? Which component makes the decision (router vs control plane)? (Ask infra-routing team)
- Are our healthchecks for the runtime too strict (causing flapping)? Thresholds are in infra repo: github.com/redwood-infra/healthchecks#runtime-checks

Short snippet for Slack handoff message (copy/paste):
"Oncall update: handled transient 5xx spike on hosted-api around 00:45. Scaled dedicated-east-1b +2, applied temporary routing overrides for non-critical routes and purged KV cache on one node. Errors returned to baseline by 01:10. Filed JIRA-INF-412 for autoscaler investigation. Please check grafana (hosted-api errors + routing-fallback) and confirm no further fallback thrash. -Maya"

Micro-tasks for next desk shift (me or next person to pick up):
- [ ] Add alert for >3 routing fallbacks in 5m
- [ ] Postmortem sketch in Confluence with timeline and logs (link to be added)
- [ ] Small PR: expose p95 as a signal for autoscaler test harness

If you find anything unexpected, tag me @maya.chen in #incidents. If slack is down, DM Diego Alvarez.

End of notes. Keep this doc ephemeral — when we have a consolidated postmortem I will archive and replace with final runbook steps.

-- maya
